target.title: fix: store usage-cost pricing fingerprint once
target.body:
Closes #99511

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with large session histories would get oversized `.usage-cost-cache.json` files because the same `pricingFingerprint` string was duplicated on every cached file entry.

## Why This Change Was Made

The usage-cost cache now stores the pricing fingerprint once at the cache-object level and bumps the cache format to version 5 so older version 4 caches rebuild cleanly. Freshness checks compare the cache-level fingerprint, and refresh clears old entries when the active pricing fingerprint changes so stale cost totals are not reused across pricing changes.

## User Impact

Large usage-cost caches are smaller and cheaper to parse/rewrite. Usage-cost totals and session summaries keep the same behavior, while older v4 cache files rebuild automatically on the next refresh.

## Evidence

- Claim proved:
  - v5 cache files serialize one top-level `pricingFingerprint` and omit per-entry copies.
  - v4 per-entry fingerprint caches rebuild into the compact v5 shape.
  - Append-only reuse and pricing invalidation still work.
  - Current-head runtime proof rebuilt a durable v4 per-entry cache through the real `loadCostUsageSummaryFromCache(..., refreshMode: "sync-when-empty")` path into the v5 compact shape.

- Commands / artifacts:
  - `node --import tsx .tmp/proof-99543-usage-cache.mjs`
    - Current head: `20e1bd2239faf3e36a74d8936fe974e46d6d864a`.
    - Isolated state dir: `C:\Users\86158\AppData\Local\Temp\openclaw-pr-99543-state-pJjGyV`.
    - Created 12 real session transcript `.jsonl` files under `agents/main/sessions`.
    - Before refresh: cache version `4`, size `35,311` bytes, entries `12`, entries with per-entry `pricingFingerprint`: `12`, top-level `pricingFingerprint`: missing.
    - After refresh: cache version `5`, size `10,420` bytes, entries `12`, entries with per-entry `pricingFingerprint`: `0`, top-level `pricingFingerprint`: present.
    - Result: `cacheStatus=fresh`, `totalTokens=1386`, removed `12` per-entry fingerprints, saved `24,891` bytes in the proof cache.
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts --reporter=verbose --testNamePattern="pricing fingerprint"`
    - Passed: `1 passed | 59 skipped`.
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts --reporter=verbose --testNamePattern="rebuilds a version 4 per-entry fingerprint cache"`
    - Passed: `1 passed | 59 skipped`.
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts --reporter=verbose --testNamePattern="invalidates durable aggregate cache when (pricing config changes|gateway pricing cache changes)|refreshes append-only durable aggregate cache"`
    - Passed: `3 passed | 57 skipped`.
  - `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD`
    - Passed.
  - `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode local`
    - Worker reported clean: no accepted/actionable findings.

- Observed result:
  - The current-head runtime proof confirmed a durable v4 cache with duplicated per-entry fingerprints rebuilds into the compact v5 shape, keeps the summary cache fresh, and removes per-entry fingerprints while preserving totals.
  - The focused regression tests confirmed the compact cache shape, v4 rebuild behavior, append-only cache reuse, and pricing-change invalidation.

- Not tested / proof gaps:
  - The full `src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts` run still has an unrelated pre-existing DST calendar failure.
  - No user-private large production cache was replayed; the runtime proof used an isolated state directory with generated OpenClaw session transcripts so no private session content was read or published.
